findings.summary: INTRODUCED BY 53e7767: every LANGUAGE-TAGGED code fence was invisible to the gate. GitHub wraps a syntax-highlighted fence in <div class="highlight highlight-source-X">, and div was on neither list, so it hid the whole subtree — observed blind for ```js ```ts ```yaml ```bash ```diff ```json ```csv ```tsv ```svg ```ipynb ```gltf. Bare ``` and ```text still worked, and those were the only two spellings the suite pinned, which is why 108/108 stayed green over it. A ```ts fence whose comment named the surface and the ADR drew THREE refusals including 'the heading is there but nothing follows it'. 3 of 38 corpus issues carry a language-tagged fence; none flipped verdict, so it was latent. Fixed in 3783db5 by allowing div.highlight* by class.

INTRODUCED BY 53e7767: every GitHub ALERT (> [!NOTE] / [!IMPORTANT] / [!WARNING]) renders as <div class="markdown-alert …"> and was blocked — GitHub's own documented callout syntax and the natural place to write what must be true. Fixed by allowing div.markdown-alert* by class.

INTRODUCED BY 53e7767: the header's ACCEPTED COST was materially understated (ADR-0051). It said the cost was 'a raw <div> an author writes by hand' and that 'markdown headings and lists are unaffected', while R5-M1 and R5-M2 are divs GitHub emits from ORDINARY markdown with no hand-written HTML. Rewritten to state exactly what is refused and what happens if GitHub adds a third visible-div class.

INTRODUCED BY 53e7767: FIVE load-bearing elements of the new walker carried no pin — blockquote and summary in COUNTED, span in TRANSPARENT, the lastIndexOf stack unwind, and the close-tag newline. Each mutation left the suite at 108 ok while flipping a real verdict against the live oracle. The unwind is the one whose loss ADMITS rather than refuses: with indexOf an inner closes the outer one and the payload after it is admitted while invisible, which is exactly the nested-div shape the enrichment scaffolding is built from. Also on record: the close-tag newline is the SAME pass the parent commit deleted as unpinnable and 53e7767 silently reinstated — it is load-bearing on compact HTML where GitHub emits no inter-tag newline, so the right action was the pin, not the deletion. All five pinned and observed red in 3783db5.

INTRODUCED BY 53e7767: the 'a blockquote criterion' pin was VACUOUS — its surface and decision sat in a paragraph AFTER the blockquote, so it passed with the quote's contents entirely hidden while reading as 'blockquote text is visible'. Payload moved inside the quote.

ruledOut: THE STAKED PREDICTION HELD. 97 attack shapes rendered through the live oracle and run through the shipped admit(), at least ~80 of them novel relative to round 4's record: ZERO admitted while invisible. Refused as they should be: all js-render-* enrichment families (mermaid, geojson, topojson, stl — every one routed through div.render-plaintext-hidden), <math-renderer> in all four spellings ($$…$$, $…$, a ```math fence, a TeX % comment), bare/uppercase/whitespaced <div> and <DIV >, nested <div> with the payload after the inner close, <div> plus a stray </section>, <ruby><rt>, <rt> alone, <pre>-in-<div>-in-<li>

the walker survives adversarial parsing: malformed nesting, mismatched close tags, attributes containing '>' inside quotes, unusual tag-name case and whitespace, unclosed tags, deep nesting — no input made it throw, and a throw would be a refusal anyway
